explication:
<explanation>
1. Identify the project type and purpose
   - Dompdf is an open-source PHP library/tool that converts HTML + CSS into PDF. It is not a standalone web application but a style-driven rendering engine composed of modular components.

2. High-level architectural overview
   - Input layer: HTML source + CSS (inline, external, CSS2.1 rules).
   - Parsing layer:
     • DOMDocument (PHP DOM extension) builds a DOM tree.
     • CSS parser (sabberworm/php-css-parser via Dompdf\Css classes) builds a style model.
   - Layout layer:
     • Frame classes build a FrameTree (DOM → FrameTree).
     • FrameReflower applies CSS box model, break points, pagination.
     • FrameDecorator augments frames with rendering attributes.
   - Rendering layer:
     • Renderer classes traverse the decorated FrameTree and emit draw commands.
     • CanvasFactory selects a Canvas adapter.
   - Canvas/Adapter layer:
     • Core “canvas” abstraction with concrete adapters for:
       – R&OS Cpdf (lib/Cpdf.php)
       – GD (for bitmapped images)
       – PDFlib (if available)
     • Canvas writes PDF primitives (text, images, shapes).
   - Output layer:
     • Final PDF stream or file is produced.
   - Supporting services:
     • FontMetrics & font loaders (php-font-lib; built-in AFM/UFM files).
     • Image handling (Dompdf\Image\Cache + GD/Imagick backends).
     • Options management (Dompdf\Options).
     • PHP evaluator for inline scripts.
     • External services: HTTP/FTP fetch of remote CSS/images (via cURL or fopen wrappers).

3. Key architectural patterns & design principles
   - Adapter pattern: Canvas/CPDF, Canvas/GD, Canvas/PDFLib.
   - Factory pattern: CanvasFactory, Frame\Factory.
   - Decorator pattern: FrameDecorator wraps Frame nodes for rendering concerns.
   - Iterator pattern: FrameListIterator, FrameTreeIterator for tree traversal.
   - Separation of concerns: parsing, styling, layout, rendering, output.

4. Drawing the system design diagram
   a. Main components & grouping (use swimlanes or distinct shapes):
      - Input: HTML source, CSS files/links.
      - Parsing & styling: DOMDocument → Dompdf\Css\Stylesheet.
      - Layout engine: FrameTree, FrameReflower, FrameDecorator.
      - Rendering engine: Renderer classes.
      - Canvas adapters: CPDF, GD, PDFlib.
      - Support modules: FontMetrics/FontLoader, Image\Cache, Options, PhpEvaluator.
   b. Relationships & data flow (directional arrows):
      - HTML/CSS → Parser → DOM + Style model → Layout → FrameTree → Decorator/Reflower → Renderer → CanvasAdapter → PDF output.
      - Renderer reads from FrameDecorator and issues commands to CanvasAdapter.
      - CanvasAdapter relies on FontMetrics + Image services.
   c. Technology labels:
      - “PHP 7.1+” runtime, DOM & MBString extensions.
      - External libs: php-font-lib, php-svg-lib, sabberworm PHP-CSS-Parser.
      - Composer autoload.
   d. Extensibility points:
      - New Canvas adapters can be added via Adapter interface.
      - Custom frame decorators or reflowers.
      - Hooks in Dompdf\Options.

5. Tailoring for this open-source tool
   - Emphasize core pipeline (parse → layout → render → output).
   - Highlight module boundaries, especially where third-party libraries integrate.
   - Show how fonts and images plug in.
   - Illustrate bin scripts (create-release.php, update-reference-output.php) as auxiliary CI tools, not part of rendering pipeline.

6. Diagram notation guidelines
   - Components as boxes or colored swimlanes:
     • Blue: core engine modules (Parser, Layout, Renderer).
     • Green: Adapters & external libraries.
     • Yellow: Supporting utilities (Fonts, Images, Options).
   - Use arrows to show data flow direction.
   - Label each arrow with the type of data (e.g., “DOM tree”, “Style model”, “Draw commands”).
   - Use different shapes (ovals for services, rectangles for modules, cylinders for storage/resources like font files).

7. Final notes
   - Be granular: break Layout into FrameFactory, FrameReflower, FrameDecorator.
   - Call out iterative processes (tree traversals) with iterators.
   - Capture configuration (Options) feeding into multiple layers.
   - Ensure font and image handling services are shown as shared dependencies.
   - Make the PDF output node the final sink with a clear arrow from the Canvas layer.
</explanation>
